6-source-1.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 of the European Parliament and of the Council on digital operational resilience in the financial sector (DORA)
6-source-1.applicability: Applies to all financial entities within the EU as defined in Article 2(1-33); establishes binding requirements for ICT incident management and classification in Articles 17 and 18

passages.text: In order to maintain full control over ICT risk, financial entities need to have comprehensive capabilities to enable a strong and effective ICT risk management, as well as specific mechanisms and policies for handling all ICT-related incidents and for reporting major ICT-related incidents.
Financial entities shall classify ICT-related incidents and shall determine their impact based on the following criteria:

6-source-2.title: Regulatory Technical Standards on criteria for the classification of ICT-related incidents
6-source-2.applicability: Official EBA technical guidance implementing RTS 2024/1772, providing operational definitions, materiality thresholds, and classification workflows for credit institutions and payment service providers

passages.text: These Regulatory Technical Standards specify the criteria for the classification of major ICT-related incidents, the approach for the classification of major incidents, the materiality thresholds of each classification criterion, the criteria and materiality thresholds for determining significant cyber threats, the criteria for competent authorities to assess the relevance of incidents to competent authorities in other Member States and the details of the incidents to be shared in this regard.

concerns.description: Requirement to establish documented ICT incident handling policies covering ownership, tracking, and response procedures for incidents affecting critical functions
Requirement to classify ICT incidents using standardized criteria and materiality thresholds distinguishing ordinary incidents, major incidents, and significant cyber threats
